text:
sam: heads-up — opened PR #4527 and CI turned red on pre-commit. I only changed docs + a tiny python import, so this feels spurious. anyone around for a quick triage?

CI Bot: build 4527 — FAILED · pre-commit hooks on ubuntu-latest · https://ci.redwood.example/runs/4527 · log attached

sam: local `pre-commit run --all-files` on my mac is green. CI output shows rustfmt + pyright failures. i'm suspicious about EOLs / platform differences. 🙃

lia: possible. did you check `git config core.autocrlf`? also run `pre-commit run --all-files --hook-stage manual` in a linux container to replicate CI env.

sam: my git shows `core.autocrlf = true`. here's the CI snippet:
```
+ /usr/bin/rustfmt --write-mode=diff src/lib.rs
Diff in src/lib.rs at line 123:
-    pub fn new()->Self{
+    pub fn new() -> Self {
```
and pyright: `src/cli.py:45: error: Optional[type] is not subscriptable (reportOptionalSubscript)`

ben: hmm — two separate issues. rustfmt diff suggests file formatting or EOLs. pyright error smells like a newer pyright version tightening rules. what pyright version locally vs CI?

sam: local pyright 1.0.280, CI reports 1.1.271 in the logs. i didn't upgrade intentionally.

jen: @ops-bot can you dump the runner image/tooling versions? might be a recent image rollout.

ops-bot: Runner metadata: ubuntu-22.04, pre-commit 2.22.1, rustfmt 1.4.37, python 3.11, pyright 1.1.271

lia: that explains pyright. For the rustfmt, try `git add --renormalize .` to fix CRLF/line endings, then run `pre-commit run rustfmt --all-files` locally in WSL/docker. If that passes, push a normalization commit.

sam: ran `git add --renormalize .` then `pre-commit run --all-files` in WSL — rustfmt failed initially, but after renormalize it now passes. pyright still errors locally when forcing pyright 1.1.271 with `npm i -g pyright@1.1.271` gave same error. stack: `Optional[str]` used maybe in typing; trying quick patch to add from typing import Optional, cast?

ben: short-term unblock: we can either pin pyright in dev deps to 1.0.x on CI or add a pyrightconfig.json override to silence `reportOptionalSubscript` for now. i'll open a follow-up. For this PR, best path is to re-run CI after normalizing EOLs so rust job is green and then we can decide on pyright fix separately.

sam: agreed. re-run requested for full pipeline? or just python job? i prefer full run to be safe.

lia: kicked full rerun: job-id-9876 (queued).

CI Bot: job-id-9876 — python & lint job SUCCEEDED; rustfmt job SUCCEEDED after normalization; overall build — PASSED.

jen: nice. on the pyright side i'll open a tiny follow-up PR that pins the CLI job to pyright 1.0.x or adds config tweak. i'll also add a checklist note to PR template: "run pre-commit in linux or WSL for multi-lang repos".

sam: thank you all! lesson learned: local mac dev with `core.autocrlf=true` can hide CI formatting issues. i'll keep an eye on pyright pinning issue.

ben: created issue #142: "pin pyright in CI and add config for Optional[] subscripts" — assigning to @jen.

sam: closing loop — CI green now, will merge after CI confirms. sorry for the ping spam and thanks for the quick help :raised_hands:

lia: awesome — nice triage flow.

jen: taking the pyright follow-up. will ping when PR is up.
